interview.openTomorrow: Yes, definitely. I'm in exam season and I need to build a consistent study routine. This timer-based challenge is exactly what I need to stay accountable and motivated.
interview.secured: I think it means locking in your commitment—like securing your streak or progress so you can't back out or lose your data. It's about making your goals permanent.
interview.freeze: I'm guessing it's a safety feature where you can pause your streak for a day without breaking it, like if you're sick or have an emergency. Lets you keep your progress intact.
interview.selfReported: That's probably where you manually log or confirm your own workout/study session since the app can't track it automatically. You're being honest about what you did.
interview.best: Seeing that 9-minute timer tick down and actually sticking with it. The visual feedback of the orange numbers was satisfying—it made the time feel real and kept me focused.
interview.worst: The blank screen in the middle felt a bit empty. I wish there was something to keep me engaged visually during the session, like a motivational quote or progress bar to break up the darkness.
interview.tellFriend: Yeah, I'd tell my study group about it. I'd say 'This app actually works—it's got a timer that forces you to commit to specific study blocks, and you can share your streak with friends. Perfect for keeping each other accountable during exam prep.'
